where: Opening film, over black
text: Months later. Days away from ORD.

where: Opening film, the company line in the afternoon
text: The outfield was behind me. I hadn't thought about any of it in a long time. I wasn't trying not to. It just went.

where: Opening film, the clearance form, the tilt to the stores
text: Last week in camp. Clear your kit, sign your papers, go home.

where: Opening film, the push-in on the figure by the stores
text: Then I saw him.

where: Play: the armskote counter, handing the rifle in
text: Rifle. Serial number... okay. In the rack, end one.

where: Play: the stores counter, handing the torch in
text: Torch, one. Sign here.

where: Play: the company office, the form signed
text: All clear. Three more days only ah. Congratulations.

where: Play: walking up to the encik
text: Encik? Encik, it's me. Hawk Company.

where: Play: he recognises him
text: Eh. You. Still alive.

where: Play: the small talk
text: Three more days, encik. Then I ORD.

where: Play: the small talk
text: Good. Go home. Eat properly, sleep properly.

where: Play: the turn — unprompted, halfway through
text: Eh. You remember the question you asked me? In the cookhouse. About the three o'clock shower.

where: The decision, option A
text: Who was it, encik? What was his story?

where: The decision, option B
text: I don't think about it anymore, encik.

where: The decision, option C
text: I think I was just too stressed.

where: The decision, option D
text: Why didn't you tell me then, encik?

where: Scene A: the recruit in bed one
text: Before my time. One recruit, bed one. Quiet boy. Every night he's the last one in the shower. He don't like people see him wash.

where: Scene A: the morning they found him
text: One morning, first parade, he's not there. They find him inside. Water still running.

where: Scene A: after
text: No note. No reason. His family come and take him back. The bunk close for one month. Then they open it again like nothing.

where: Scene A: the attachment line — the episode's teaching
text: Since then, every batch, bed one, three o'clock. Sometimes the departed are still stuck at the places they have attachments to. That shower was his.

where: Scene A: and he closes it
text: You asked, so I told you. But don't go and make it into something. He's not your business.

where: Scene B: the nod
text: Good. Better than me.

where: Scene B: his own night in that bunk
text: I was in that bunk also. I went to look once. Water running. Somebody standing under it, back facing me. I went back to bed and never look again. One month, then nothing.

where: Scene B: why he said nothing in the cookhouse
text: That morning in the cookhouse I say nothing, because if I tell you, you check every night until ORD. You didn't.

where: Scene B: the line that closes the episode
text: After your batch posted out. Quiet. First time in years.

where: Scene C: the whole scene
text: I know it is easier to brush things off with logic and reason. But there are many things you simply won't fully understand.

where: Scene D: the boy he told once
text: Because I told one boy before you. Same question. After that he checked every night. Two months later he's out. Not sick. Not injured. Just cannot anymore.

where: Scene D: the rule he made after
text: After him I decide. Nobody gets told until they are leaving.

where: Scene D: and the quiet
text: After your batch posted out. Quiet. First time in years. Now you know. Now it cannot hurt you.

where: Under outcome card A
text: I asked who he was. Encik told me, and then told me to leave it there.

where: Under outcome card B
text: I had already let it go. He only confirmed I was right to.

where: Under outcome card C
text: I called it stress. He wouldn't let me.

where: Under outcome card D
text: I wanted a reason I was owed. He gave me one. It didn't help.

where: The closing narration, to camera, in all four outcomes
text: The departed stay where their attachments are. So do the living. His was that shower. Mine was the question. When I put it down, so did he.
